description: Build the player-facing UI on top of FEAT-003's APIs: Red/Blue lobby and queue pages, the live match view (attack console, log-tail/patch console, team activity feeds), the spectator/results view with the live Central Vault counter, tension meter and SSE event feed, the End-of-Match After Action Report, and per-team/per-player leaderboards. Depends entirely on FEAT-003's routes existing and returning real data; this feature is UI-only, no new backend logic beyond simple read-only leaderboard queries.
steps: Add src/app/range/page.tsx and src/app/range/lobby/page.tsx (client components, following the fetch+useState+useEffect polling style of src/app/demo/matchmaking/page.tsx and src/app/demo/team/page.tsx) for choosing/joining a Red or Blue queue for a level/room and showing who else is queued; call the new /api/range/queue route from FEAT-003.

Add src/app/range/match/[matchId]/page.tsx as the live match view: render the Red attack console (a form posting to /api/range/[matchId]/proxy and showing the raw response) or the Blue patch console + log-tail (editing files via /api/range/[matchId]/patch and viewing the SSE event stream) depending on the current user's side for that match, resolved server-side before rendering via the same team-membership query pattern already used in the API routes.

Add a reusable client hook/component for consuming the SSE route (new src/components/range/useRangeEvents.ts using EventSource against /api/range/[matchId]/events) and a live feed component styled after the existing src/components/visuals/LogStream.tsx and src/components/visuals/AlertQueue.tsx (color-coded by team, timestamped, auto-scrolling) — reuse those components' visual style/approach rather than inventing a new one from scratch.

Add the Central Vault balance ticker and tension meter (new src/components/range/VaultMeter.tsx) driven purely by the SSE feed's vault_balance_cents updates, no client-side animation timers faking progress.

Add src/app/range/spectate/[matchId]/page.tsx: the read-only spectator view (vault balance, combined event feed, running score), gated only by requireUser via the shared src/app/range/layout.tsx (no team-membership check, consistent with 'anyone logged in, not playing' from the spec).

Add src/app/range/match/[matchId]/report/page.tsx: the After Action Report, fetching a new read-only src/app/api/range/[matchId]/report/route.ts (GET, requires login, no team-membership restriction once the match has ended) that returns final score, vault survived/drained, MVP per team (from FEAT-003's audit_logs aggregation), and the full event timeline for that match — render as the 'shareable, impressive artifact' screen.

Add src/app/range/leaderboard/page.tsx + src/app/api/range/leaderboard/route.ts (GET, login-only) aggregating per-team and per-player (by username/name, never email) stats across all ended range_target_matches, optionally filterable by level/room.
acceptance_criteria: a logged-out visitor hitting any /range/** URL is redirected to login (via the existing requireUser redirect behavior), never shown range content
the live match view renders the correct console (attack vs patch) based on the viewer's actual team/side for that match and never based on client-supplied state
the vault meter and event feed update in the browser purely from real SSE events sent by the server, verified by triggering a real exploit/patch in a manual end-to-end run and watching the UI update
the After Action Report page renders a complete real summary (final score, vault balance, MVP per team, timeline) for a match that has actually ended
leaderboards show usernames/names only, never emails, confirmed by inspecting the rendered page source and the report/leaderboard API responses
verification: PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm run build — full Next.js production build succeeds with the new pages/routes (never run while `npm run dev` is active)
PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm test — unaffected, still passing

manual end-to-end run (documented in the final report): seed 2 red + 2 blue test users directly in the DB (same seeding helpers tests use), drive them through queue -> match -> at least one real exploit via the proxy route and one real patch via the patch route -> match end, and capture the resulting After Action Report JSON/page as evidence
git commit this section's changes as one commit
findings: UI added under src/app/range: page.tsx (hub), lobby/page.tsx (client, polls GET /api/range/queue every 3s, POST to queue, redirects to match when paired/active), match/[matchId]/page.tsx (server: getCurrentUser + getMatchAccess decides side; redirects non-members to /range/lobby and ended matches to report; Blue gets server.js/db.js source read from range-target/ as editor start), match/[matchId]/report/page.tsx, spectate/[matchId]/page.tsx (any logged-in user; 404 if not a range match), leaderboard/page.tsx. Components in src/components/range: useRangeEvents (EventSource, ?role=spectator), RangeFeed, VaultMeter (pure SSE-driven), AttackConsole, PatchConsole, MatchView, SpectatorView. New backend (read-only): GET /api/range/queue (my team, active session id, waiting squads by team name), GET /api/range/<id>/report (login only, 404 until match_sessions not ACTIVE), GET /api/range/leaderboard; queries in src/lib/range-runtime/reports.ts (buildReport/buildLeaderboard, DB only, names never emails; timeline excludes RANGE_CONTAINER_LOG; score = counts of EXPLOIT_LANDED/EXPLOIT_BLOCKED/PATCH_APPLIED; vault start constant 50,000,000). No level/room filter on the leaderboard (no such concept exists). Layout/guards/session/middleware untouched. Ran (PATH=.tools/node22/bin): npm run build -> OK, all new routes/pages listed; npm test -> 47/47; real HTTP e2e via .agents/tasks/fintech-range/e2e/run.sh (next start on :3457, DB .test.sqlite.e2e, seeds 2 red+2 blue+1 spectator): logged-out /range/lobby -> 307 /demo/login; blue queued, spectator saw queue, red pairing created a real container (status RUNNING); match page for red shows Attack console, blue shows Patch console, non-member redirected; blue calling proxy and red calling patch -> 403; real exploit via proxy (open admin), real patch via patch route (-> exploit BLOCKED), boss vault sweep -> vault 0 -> match ended winner RED; report JSON (saved in e2e/report-evidence.json) has score 2 landed/1 blocked/1 patch, MVPs RedOne/BlueOne, full timeline; leaderboard shows teams and players by name; zero '@' in report/leaderboard JSON and zero e2e emails in rendered report/leaderboard/spectate HTML; SSE for red/blue/spectator delivered vault + audit + end events, spectator stream had no PROXY_REQUEST/PATCH_APPLIED. Not done: no headless browser, so the React client behaviour (EventSource rendering) was not driven in a browser; the SSE stream and server-rendered pages were verified over HTTP only. Fixed during e2e: report timeline scope/details parsing for RED/BLUE tags. docker ps -a / network ls with label cynchor.range empty afterwards; next start process stopped.
